P0.definition: frozen positive predictor slope, exact reanchor
P0.interpretation: fixed-point consistency does not provide nonlinear robustness

P1.definition: exact physical derivative p(y), Newton relinearized every iterate
P1.interpretation: root convergence alone hides an unacceptable unsafeguarded excursion

P2.interpretation: robust in the tested NH03 starts but slow because root |rho| is about 0.863

P3.definition: frozen positive P0 raw update plus alpha(y)=1/(1-rho(y)), constrained to 0<alpha<=1
P3.interpretation: where alpha is admissible and exact p is known, the relaxed P0 step is algebraically the Newton step; it is not an independent robustness mechanism

P4.definition: physical Newton plus factor-1/2 contraction until physical branch and non-increasing absolute residual
P4.interpretation: safeguarding removes the large Newton excursion while preserving the exact root

conclusions: A frozen positive surrogate can fail badly in a nonlinear response even though exact reanchoring preserves the coupled fixed point.

Physical Newton is locally fast but root convergence is insufficient as a robustness criterion because an unsafeguarded step can leave the hydrologically meaningful neighborhood by orders of magnitude.
Picard provides a robust baseline in this NH03 case but is too slow to be the preferred general policy.
Response-derived relaxation is principled in the local affine sense, but when exact p is used it collapses algebraically to Newton and can require alpha>1 outside the allowed relaxation range.
Safeguarded physical Newton is the only tested G04 policy combining fast convergence with bounded difficult-start behavior.
production_disposition: NO_PRODUCTION_ADMISSION. G04 is analytical nonlinear evidence; real-SWAP nonlinear/window/regime qualification remains required.
